sections.h2: Grain now supplies 72.47% of allocated ethanol, cane 27.52%

chart.title: Surplus FCI rice outsupplies direct sugarcane juice, 22.25% against 15.82%
chart.sub: Share of allocated ethanol volume, ESY 2025-26 cycle 1, %.
chart.source: OMC allocation for ESY 2025-26 cycle 1, as reported by ChiniMandi.

sections.means: Grain-based feedstocks carry nearly three quarters of the allocated volume, so cane is now the minority supplier.
sections.todo: Track the FCI rice release price and the mechanism that decides how much rice goes to distilleries rather than the public distribution system.

sections.h2: Maize rose from 6.2% to 45.68% of ethanol feedstock in three supply years

chart.title: Maize's share of ethanol feedstock climbed from 6.2% to 45.68% in three years
chart.sub: Maize share of allocated ethanol volume, %.
chart.source: Original post; OMC allocation for ESY 2025-26 cycle 1, as reported by ChiniMandi.

sections.means: Maize moved from a marginal feedstock to the largest one in three supply years, driven by availability rather than by a maize-specific programme.
sections.todo: Watch maize acreage and imports, since a domestic shortfall would turn import substitution into an import line.

sections.h2: Distillers offered 1,776 crore litres, and 1,048 were allocated

chart.title: Allocation covered 59% of offered capacity, leaving 728 crore litres unbought
chart.sub: Ethanol volume for ESY 2025-26 cycle 1, crore litres.
chart.source: Original post; OMC allocation for ESY 2025-26 cycle 1, as reported by ChiniMandi.

sections.means: Distillers have more capacity than oil companies are buying, so the marginal plant now competes for an allocation rather than being courted for output.
sections.todo: Watch whether the 728 crore litres of idle capacity drives a push for a higher blending mandate before any feedstock question arises.
